stories.summary: The obsolete PixelPlanets scene integration and dangling symlink were removed, with deterministic contract smoke coverage added. The implementation packet was archived, but its preserved independent review is held by strict source-scope validation. A separate narrowly scoped correction/review pair has now entered ready/auto metadata.
stories.body: The source migration landed at 25a7f6d1 and its implementation packet was archived at 5991a89b. It removes the obsolete PixelPlanets scene dependency while retaining deterministic planet identity and world profiles, and adds a focused smoke test. The preserved independent review did not obtain a PASS: its documented source scope omitted the new smoke and validation-manifest paths, so host pre-launch validation stopped. A dedicated exact-scope attestation correction and independent review were authored at 98c2b7f5 and marked ready/auto at 761ea680. Those states are GitHub metadata, not proof of running or acceptance. No host teardown was verified. Canonical dispatcher totals and fresh private operational observations are unavailable.

sections.heading: The migration is real, not merely queued
sections.text: The landed change removes the legacy planet scene and dangling symlink, retains deterministic planet selection and environmental profiles, and adds a focused contract smoke test. sections.heading: A narrow evidence correction is now queued

A new correction must attest exactly the missing smoke-test and validation-manifest paths without weakening the broader source-integrity gate. Its own independent reviewer is a separate required step. Both correction packets are now marked ready/auto, not verified running.

insights.title: The blocker is evidence provenance, not a requested planet redesign

insights.title: The correction must itself pass independent scrutiny
insights.explanation: A narrowly scoped attestation can unblock the original review only after the correction receives its own genuine independent acceptance. Neither ready/auto metadata nor successful implementation tests substitute for that verdict.

stories.headline: Crèche gets a layered 3D-rendered art blueprint, but no new assets yet
stories.summary: A design-only Crèche manifest now defines 30 proposed visual states, including 22 required and eight optional, for a realistic PBR-rendered 2D scene. Existing gameplay and art registration remain unchanged; visual approvals and production are still ahead.
stories.body: Commit 0d41ea40 publishes a Crèche layered PBR design manifest with depth bands from exterior and floor through fixtures, local effects and foreground occlusion. It preserves Godot's existing 2D gameplay and collision ownership while specifying orthographic 3D-rendered art, source registration and animation states. The 30 states are design inventory, not completed assets. The commit explicitly says no Asset V2 registry change, human visual approval or runtime cutover occurred. Commit message reports GitHub Validate Repository PASS, but the combined status endpoint returned no checks; independent validation was not verified. Operational dispatcher totals remain unavailable.

article.lead: The Crèche of Answerless Names has a more precise visual production blueprint. A new manifest describes how to build realistic, depth-separated scenery and animation without replacing CUSTODIAN's existing 2D gameplay. It is a design milestone, not an art delivery.

sections.heading: Real depth without a gameplay-engine migration
sections.text: The proposal uses orthographic renders of modeled stone, metal and machinery, split into floor, structural, fixture, effect and foreground layers. Godot keeps ownership of movement, collision and interactions.

insights.title: Layer separation makes animation practical
insights.explanation: Keeping machines, floor and foreground occlusion independent allows localized effects and character overlap without repainting the entire room for every animation frame.

article.next_watch: Watch for approved first source plates, registered Asset V2 states and an in-game validation showing correct alpha, depth and interaction alignment.

stories.headline: Browser reply reader lands with unfinished return paths
stories.summary: A new read-only ChatGPT browser adapter landed on main to help CUSTODIAN orchestration collect completed replies. Code inspection finds debugging return paths that break its stated output contract; validation and live operation are not established.
stories.body: Commit f42cc51 adds get_chatgpt_response.py v1.1.0, attaching through an existing local Chrome debugging endpoint and reading visible conversation DOM. The implementation documents a strict completed-text / RESPONSE IN PROGRESS / error contract, but read_once currently returns 'FIRST DOT GET BUSY' when generation is active, returns a page object when reply text is empty, and emits a debugging placeholder on an unexpected probe result. These paths contradict the documented interface and may confuse orchestration consumers. This is a verified source-level defect, not proof of an observed runtime failure. No tests, independent acceptance, running process, or teardown were verified. The private pilot observation pointer was last modified earlier than this commit and is not fresh evidence of this state.
bullets: Read-only browser reply adapter added to main.
Three return paths conflict with its documented stdout contract.
No runtime failure or CI success inferred from source alone.
Correct contract branches and validate before wiring into orchestration.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN now has a browser-side reader intended to collect completed ChatGPT responses for its orchestration loop. The new script is on main, but its current source contains unfinished return paths that could mislead the next automation step.

sections.heading: A bridge from browser conversations to orchestration
sections.text: The adapter attaches to an existing Chrome debugging session, identifies a conversation and reads visible assistant text. It is designed to avoid private application APIs and report whether a reply has finished.

sections.heading: The contract and the code diverge
sections.text: The script promises either completed text, a standard in-progress marker, or a nonzero error. Instead, an active reply can return a debugging phrase; an empty reply can return a browser page object; and an unexpected probe state returns a placeholder. These are source-confirmed inconsistencies, not observed production failures.

insights.title: A small protocol mismatch can stall a large art pipeline
insights.explanation: An orchestrator needs reliable completion signals before fetching and installing generated assets. Ambiguous output can turn a finished response into a false success or a stuck handoff.

insights.title: Landing is not validation
insights.explanation: The commit proves the adapter exists on main. It does not establish tests, independent acceptance, or a running browser connection.

article.takeaway: The new bridge is a useful integration point, but its response contract needs correction and tests before consumers rely on it.
article.next_watch: Watch for a follow-up patch restoring the documented return values and a bounded test of completed, streaming, empty, and ambiguous replies.
